architecture.semanticTags: Build/mechanic recommendation meaning only; restricted to the frozen certified feat/talent-used tag union.
architecture.ruleSelectors: Exact canonical identity, weapon family, group, proficiency, attack-profile, and named ability applicability.
architecture.comparisonProfile: Damage, stun, hands, double-weapon behavior, reach, ranged secondary profiles, defensive utility, control utility, and mounted/mobility role relative to Vibroblade.
architecture.missingIdentityRule: Phase 3B unmapped identities remain explicit canonical identities with repoIdentityKey=null. This pass does not invent or write production records.
architecture.weaponDeclarationPrinciple: Weapons declare what they are; abilities declare what they apply to.

source.book: Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: Medium 2d6 vibroblade intended for two-handed use. A Medium wielder using it two-handed applies double the wielder's Strength bonus to damage. It requires an energy cell.

rationale.melee: Its canonical attack profile is melee.
rationale.offense_melee: It deals direct 2d6 slashing or piercing melee damage.
rationale.damage_bonus: The source explicitly gives a Medium two-handed wielder double Strength bonus to damage.

relativeToVibroblade.recommendationFit: Strength-focused two-handed melee option for characters who want a conventional vibroblade profile with stronger ability-modifier scaling.

unrepresentedMechanics.mechanic: Two-handed Strength scaling is conditional on wielder/use state.

source.book: Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: Large double weapon dealing 2d6 with each end. Attacking with both ends uses the normal full-round double-weapon attack rules and penalties. It requires two energy cells.

rationale.offense_melee: Each end deals direct 2d6 slashing melee damage.
rationale.double_weapon: It is explicitly a double weapon.
rationale.full_attack: Using both ends is performed through the double-weapon full-attack rules.

relativeToVibroblade.recommendationFit: Dedicated double-weapon choice for full-attack builds. Prefer when the character invests in double-weapon penalty reduction and multiattack support.

unrepresentedMechanics.mechanic: Both attack rolls take the normal double-weapon penalty before feat/talent reductions.
unrepresentedMechanics.note: Do not encode the base penalty as a negative semantic tag.

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: Medium 2d8 bludgeoning/energy pole weapon with a same-as-base stun setting. It can be thrown like a javelin. Gungans proficient with simple weapons are also proficient with it. It requires two energy cells.

rationale.offense_melee: It deals 2d8 bludgeoning/energy damage in melee.
rationale.ranged: It has an explicit thrown ranged profile.
rationale.offense_ranged: The thrown profile deals the same direct damage at range.
rationale.stun: It has a same-as-base 2d8 stun setting.
rationale.nonlethal: The stun setting provides a nonlethal option.

selectorGuardrails: Do not add forbidden semantic tag `thrown`; thrown behavior is structural.
Gungan simple-weapon proficiency is an alternate proficiency rule, not a semantic tag.

relativeToVibroblade.recommendationFit: Versatile melee/thrown weapon with strong base damage and stun. Especially attractive to Gungans because of the alternate proficiency rule.

unrepresentedMechanics.note: Keep racial proficiency logic outside semantic tags.

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: Large 2d6/2d6 double weapon. Either end can deal normal or 2d6 stun damage. Phrik construction gives the weapon itself DR 20, including against lightsaber attacks. It requires two energy cells.

rationale.melee: Both staff ends are melee profiles.
rationale.offense_melee: Each end deals direct 2d6 bludgeoning/energy damage.
rationale.double_weapon: It is explicitly a double weapon.
rationale.full_attack: Both ends participate in double-weapon full attacks.
rationale.stun: Either end can be set to 2d6 stun.
rationale.durability: The weapon itself has exceptional phrik durability.
rationale.damage_reduction: The electrostaff explicitly has DR 20, even against lightsaber attacks.

relativeToVibroblade.recommendationFit: Durable double-weapon platform for full-attack users who also want strong nonlethal flexibility and a weapon that resists lightsaber damage.

unrepresentedMechanics.mechanic: DR 20 belongs to the weapon object, not the wielder.
unrepresentedMechanics.note: Recommendation semantics must not imply the character gains DR 20.

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: Large 2d8 piercing/energy mounted lance. A Ride-trained Medium rider can wield it one-handed while mounted; a Medium wielder using it unmounted takes -1 to attacks. It also fires a plasma bolt as a no-stun blaster carbine and both profiles function underwater.

rationale.melee: Its lance thrust is a melee attack.
rationale.offense_melee: The lance deals direct 2d8 piercing/energy melee damage.
rationale.ranged: It has a separate plasma-bolt ranged profile.
rationale.offense_ranged: The plasma profile functions as a damaging blaster carbine without stun.
rationale.sustained_damage: The blaster-carbine profile inherits single/autofire functionality.
rationale.mount: Its handling rules explicitly improve while mounted.
rationale.ride: The one-handed mounted benefit requires training in Ride.
rationale.rider: It is purpose-built for a mounted wielder.

selectorGuardrails: Underwater operation is structured environment metadata; do not invent an `aquatic` semantic tag.
Ranged plasma mode uses Rifle proficiency because it functions as a blaster carbine.

relativeToVibroblade.recommendationFit: Hybrid cavalry weapon for Ride-trained mounted characters who want both melee striking and rifle-class ranged fire from one platform.

unrepresentedMechanics.mechanic: Medium unmounted wielders take -1 to attacks; Ride-trained Medium mounted wielders can use it one-handed.
Both melee and ranged profiles function underwater.
unrepresentedMechanics.note: No aquatic semantic tag is introduced.

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: Medium 2d8 piercing/energy pole weapon with lethal and 2d8 stun settings. It requires two energy cells.

rationale.melee: Its canonical attack profile is melee.
rationale.offense_melee: It deals direct 2d8 piercing/energy melee damage.
rationale.stun: The power dial provides an explicit 2d8 stun setting.

relativeToVibroblade.recommendationFit: Straightforward high-damage advanced melee weapon with a strong stun option; a broadly useful nonlethal alternative to the baseline Vibroblade.

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: Large 2d12 gravity-assisted hammer. Power Attack extra damage applies to objects and vehicles when used with it. Double Attack, Triple Attack, and Rapid Strike each impose an additional -2 attack penalty. It requires two energy cells.

rationale.offense_melee: It deals very high direct 2d12 bludgeoning damage.
rationale.vehicle: Its explicit Power Attack interaction extends extra damage to vehicles, making anti-vehicle use a real mechanical role.

explicitAbilityLinks.effect: Power Attack extra damage can apply to objects and vehicles when using the Power Hammer.

relativeToVibroblade.recommendationFit: Heavy single-hit and anti-object/anti-vehicle option. Excellent for Power Attack builds; deliberately poor for Double Attack, Triple Attack, and Rapid Strike users because of the extra -2 penalty.

unrepresentedMechanics.mechanic: Power Attack's extra damage is external ability synergy, not an intrinsic permanent damage bonus.
unrepresentedMechanics.note: Do not add `damage_bonus` solely from owning the weapon.

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: Large 2d8 bludgeoning/energy mounted lance. It retains the Energy Lance's Ride-trained one-handed mounted handling and the -1 Medium-unmounted penalty, but has no plasma-bolt firing mode.

rationale.offense_melee: It deals direct 2d8 bludgeoning/energy damage.
rationale.mount: Its wielding rules explicitly improve while mounted.
rationale.ride: The one-handed mounted handling requires training in Ride.
rationale.rider: It is designed for mounted cavalry and speeder-bike scouts.

relativeToVibroblade.recommendationFit: Melee-only cavalry weapon for Ride-trained mounted characters who want the Energy Lance's mounted handling without paying for a ranged profile.

unrepresentedMechanics.mechanic: Medium unmounted wielder -1 attack; Ride-trained Medium mounted wielder can use it one-handed.

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: Large 2d6 double staff. It can be used with Block as though it were a lightsaber. On each attack the wielder may choose to deal stun instead of lethal damage. It requires two energy cells.

rationale.melee: Both ends are melee attack profiles.
rationale.offense_melee: The staff deals direct 2d6 energy/bludgeoning damage.
rationale.double_weapon: It is explicitly a double weapon.
rationale.full_attack: Its two ends support double-weapon full attacks.
rationale.stun: The wielder may declare stun damage on each individual attack.
rationale.nonlethal: The per-attack stun choice provides strong nonlethal flexibility.
rationale.block: The source explicitly allows it to be used with Block as though it were a lightsaber.

explicitAbilityLinks.effect: May use Block with the San-Ni Staff as though it were a lightsaber.

selectorGuardrails: Block compatibility does not make the weapon a lightsaber and does not imply other lightsaber-only abilities apply.

relativeToVibroblade.recommendationFit: Defensive double-weapon option for Block users who want full-attack capability and per-attack lethal/stun flexibility without using a lightsaber.

unrepresentedMechanics.mechanic: Stun choice is made per attack rather than as a persistent weapon setting.

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: Large melee weapon dealing native 3d6 stun only. If pre-halving stun damage equals or exceeds a susceptible target's current hit points, the target moves -5 condition-track steps and falls unconscious. It can mount as a rifle bayonet; proficiency with that rifle removes the advanced-melee nonproficiency penalty for the mounted shock stick.

rationale.offense_melee: It makes direct melee stun attacks.
rationale.stun: It always deals native 3d6 stun damage.
rationale.nonlethal: It is a dedicated nonlethal disabling weapon.
rationale.control: A sufficiently strong hit can immediately force -5 condition-track steps and unconsciousness.
rationale.battlefield_control: Its disabling effect can remove a vulnerable opponent from effective combat.

selectorGuardrails: The rifle-bayonet proficiency waiver is configuration-specific; it does not globally change the weapon's proficiency category.
Do not add forbidden semantic tag `condition_track`; use control/battlefield_control and preserve the exact track effect structurally.

profileSelectors.condition: mounted on rifle AND wielder proficient with that rifle

relativeToVibroblade.recommendationFit: Dedicated stun/control weapon, especially attractive as a rifle-mounted bayonet or for characters who want to disable weakened targets rather than kill them.

unrepresentedMechanics.mechanic: If pre-halving stun damage >= current HP, target moves -5 condition-track steps and becomes unconscious.
unrepresentedMechanics.note: Exact threshold and effect remain structured.

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: Small reach-2 shock whip dealing 1d6 bludgeoning damage. After a hit it can make a free no-grab-penalty grab attack against a target no more than one size larger. Once per turn, a swift action automatically deals 2d6 energy damage to a target grabbed by the whip. With Trip, the wielder may knock the target prone instead of grabbing it.

rationale.offense_melee: It deals direct melee damage.
rationale.positioning: Reach 2 squares materially changes melee threat distance.
rationale.grab: A successful hit can immediately trigger a no-penalty grab attack.
rationale.control: The grab locks the weapon onto a target and restricts target handling.
rationale.battlefield_control: Reach plus grab/trip options shape enemy positioning and options.
rationale.swift_action: The grabbed-target shock is activated as a swift action.
rationale.action_economy: The weapon adds both a free-action follow-up grab and a swift-action damage option.
rationale.sustained_damage: A grabbed target can take automatic 2d6 energy damage once per turn without another attack roll.

explicitAbilityLinks.effect: After a hit, Trip may replace the whip's optional grab and knock the target prone.

damage.canonical: 1d6 hit + optional recurring 2d6 energy while grabbed

relativeToVibroblade.recommendationFit: Control-oriented reach weapon for characters built around grabs, Trip, positioning, and action-efficient sustained pressure rather than raw first-hit damage.

unrepresentedMechanics.mechanic: Free follow-up grab uses a second attack at normal bonus and ignores the normal -5 grab penalty; weapon cannot attack another target while maintaining the grab.
unrepresentedMechanics.note: Preserve target-size limit and weapon-lock state explicitly.

source.book: Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: Large 2d6/2d6 phrik double weapon. It can deal stun equal to normal damage and can be switched to stun as a swift action. Its phrik construction prevents lightsabers from ignoring the weapon's damage reduction, though this source does not state the DR value. It uses two energy cells.

rationale.offense_melee: Each end deals 2d6 bludgeoning/energy damage.
rationale.double_weapon: It is explicitly a double weapon.
rationale.full_attack: Both ends can be used in the normal double-weapon full attack.
rationale.stun: It can deal stun equal to normal damage.
rationale.nonlethal: The stun setting provides a nonlethal mode.
rationale.swift_action: Changing to stun is explicitly a swift action.
rationale.action_economy: Mode switching has a combat action cost.
rationale.durability: Phrik construction gives special resistance against lightsaber damage.
rationale.damage_reduction: The weapon's DR remains applicable against lightsabers rather than being bypassed.

selectorGuardrails: Do not invent a numeric DR value; KOTOR establishes lightsaber resistance to its DR but does not state the number.

relativeToVibroblade.recommendationFit: Full-attack/stun double weapon for users who also care about the weapon surviving lightsaber contact.

unrepresentedMechanics.mechanic: The source establishes that lightsabers do not ignore the shockstaff's DR but does not state its numeric DR.
unrepresentedMechanics.note: Never borrow Electrostaff DR 20 without separate authority.

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: Large 2d6 piercing/energy reach pike with lethal and 2d6 stun settings. It can also be thrown like a spear and requires an energy cell.

rationale.offense_melee: It deals direct 2d6 piercing/energy melee damage.
rationale.positioning: It is explicitly a reach weapon.
rationale.ranged: It can be thrown like a spear.
rationale.offense_ranged: Thrown use provides direct weapon damage at range.
rationale.stun: It has an explicit 2d6 stun setting.
rationale.nonlethal: The stun setting provides a nonlethal attack mode.

selectorGuardrails: Do not add forbidden semantic tag `thrown`; throwing is a structural quality/profile.

relativeToVibroblade.recommendationFit: Versatile reach/stun/thrown pike for characters who want control of melee distance plus a fallback ranged attack.

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: Large 2d10 slashing vibro-ax powered by two energy cells. It has no special attack mode beyond its high base cutting damage.

rationale.offense_melee: It deals direct 2d10 slashing melee damage.

relativeToVibroblade.recommendationFit: Straightforward high-damage melee option. Prefer when raw single-hit damage matters more than stun, reach, double-weapon, or utility features.

unrepresentedMechanics.note: Raw larger dice alone do not justify `damage_bonus`.

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: Powered rifle bayonet dealing 2d6 piercing damage when mounted. Even after using the rifle for a ranged attack on the previous turn, the wielder still threatens adjacent squares and can make attacks of opportunity. Mounted use requires two hands and is incompatible with a folded stock. Detached, it functions as a Vibrodagger.

rationale.melee: The bayonet provides a melee attack profile.
rationale.offense_melee: Mounted use deals 2d6 piercing melee damage.
rationale.attack_of_opportunity: It explicitly preserves melee threat and attacks of opportunity even after the rifle was used for a ranged attack.

profileSelectors.condition: rifle stock not folded; two-handed use
profileSelectors.effect: 2d6 piercing melee; preserves threat/AoO after ranged fire

relativeToVibroblade.recommendationFit: Excellent rifle-sidearm integration for characters who need to preserve melee threat and opportunity attacks without switching away from their rifle.

unrepresentedMechanics.mechanic: Mounted/detached state changes its effective weapon identity and handling.
unrepresentedMechanics.note: Detached state should resolve as Vibrodagger behavior.

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: Small 2d6 slashing-or-piercing powered melee weapon. It has no stun, reach, double-weapon, ranged, or other special combat profile and requires an energy cell.

rationale.offense_melee: Deals direct 2d6 slashing or piercing melee damage.

relativeToVibroblade.recommendationFit: Default Advanced Melee choice when no specialized weapon aligns more closely with the character's build.

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: Large 2d6/2d6 double vibroblade powered by two energy cells. Both ends can attack in a full-round action using the normal double-weapon penalties before feat/talent reductions.

rationale.offense_melee: Each end deals 2d6 slashing damage.
rationale.double_weapon: It is explicitly a double weapon.
rationale.full_attack: Both ends are used through a full-round double-weapon attack.

selectorGuardrails: Keep this Phase 3B identity distinct from KOTOR's `Double Vibroblade` until identity normalization explicitly merges them.

relativeToVibroblade.recommendationFit: Dedicated double-weapon full-attack platform. Mechanically similar to KOTOR's Double Vibroblade but retained as a separate canonical Phase 3B identity.

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: Tiny 2d4 slashing-or-piercing vibro weapon that can be thrown and is lightly regulated because it is commonly treated as a tool. It requires an energy cell.

rationale.offense_melee: Deals direct 2d4 melee damage.
rationale.offense_ranged: Thrown use provides direct ranged offense.

selectorGuardrails: Do not add `concealment` or `stealth` merely from Tiny size/light regulation; no source mechanical concealment benefit is stated.
Do not add forbidden `thrown` semantic tag.

relativeToVibroblade.recommendationFit: Compact throwable vibro option for characters who value portability and a melee/ranged fallback over raw damage.

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: Worn vibro weapon that adds +3 damage to successful unarmed attacks. While worn, attacks count both as normal unarmed/simple-weapon attacks and as Advanced Melee attacks. The knucklers cannot be disarmed or dropped and require an energy cell.

rationale.offense_melee: They increase direct melee damage.
rationale.unarmed: Their entire function is to enhance unarmed attacks.
rationale.martial_arts: They directly support unarmed/martial-arts combat builds while preserving unarmed status.
rationale.damage_bonus: They explicitly add +3 damage to a successful unarmed attack.

profileSelectors.effect: +3 damage; cannot be disarmed or dropped

relativeToVibroblade.recommendationFit: Premier Advanced Melee option for unarmed/Martial Arts builds because it adds damage without making the attack cease to count as unarmed.

unrepresentedMechanics.mechanic: Attacks simultaneously count as unarmed/simple and Advanced Melee; item cannot be disarmed or dropped.

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: Large 2d10 piercing-or-slashing reach vibro polearm. It is explicitly too large and unwieldy to throw effectively and requires an energy cell.

rationale.melee: Its only combat profile is melee.
rationale.offense_melee: Deals high 2d10 piercing or slashing melee damage.
rationale.positioning: It is explicitly a reach weapon.

selectorGuardrails: Source explicitly says it cannot be thrown effectively; do not infer a thrown profile from its lance form.

relativeToVibroblade.recommendationFit: High-damage reach weapon for front-line characters who want superior melee spacing without a thrown or stun option.

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: Medium 2d6 slashing vibro weapon designed to suppress the ultrasonic noise of normal vibro weapons, making it completely silent in use. It requires two energy cells.

rationale.offense_melee: Deals direct 2d6 slashing damage.
rationale.stealth: The source explicitly makes the weapon completely silent in use.
rationale.infiltration: Silent operation materially supports covert use and avoids weapon-noise disclosure.

relativeToVibroblade.recommendationFit: Covert melee alternative to the baseline Vibroblade: same damage role, but completely silent in operation.

unrepresentedMechanics.note: Stealth/infiltration describe recommendation relevance; exact silence remains a source rule.

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: Large 2d8 slashing-or-piercing oversized vibroblade intended for two-handed use. It requires an energy cell.

rationale.offense_melee: It deals direct 2d8 slashing or piercing damage.

relativeToVibroblade.recommendationFit: Straightforward two-handed damage upgrade over the standard Vibroblade, with no additional control, stun, reach, or defensive utility.

unrepresentedMechanics.mechanic: Source describes it as intended for two-handed use but grants no separate special damage multiplier beyond normal rules.
